Thermal designSummer 2026

Hydrogen Peroxide Tank
Thermal Management

A passive cooling concept connecting a spacecraft propellant tank to an external radiator through an aluminum saddle and heat pipes.

  • Fusion 360
  • Excel
  • Heat transfer
Read project

During my summer internship at Manastu Space Technologies, I worked on a passive cooling concept for a spacecraft's hydrogen-peroxide propellant tank. The goal was to move heat from the tank to an external radiator while keeping the propellant within its required temperature range.

I started by sizing the tank from the usable propellant requirement and blowdown conditions, then built the assembly in Fusion 360. I used rounded ends and a cylindrical middle section to leave room for mounting and thermal contact. An aluminum saddle collected heat from the tank, and heat pipes carried it to the radiator through a removable mechanical interface.

To assess the design, I calculated heat transfer through the tube connections and radiation between the tank and surrounding spacecraft surfaces. I also considered sunlight and Earth radiation at the external radiator. A thermal-resistance model helped me trace the full heat-transfer path and see how geometry, contact area, and interface materials affected the temperature difference.

The result was a CAD concept and technical report that supported preliminary hot-case feasibility. Hardware performance and cold-case control still needed further verification. This project gave me experience turning thermal calculations into a mechanical design and identifying which assumptions needed to be checked next.

Mechanical integrationSummer 2026

Xenon Tank Packaging
& Feasibility

A compact electric-propulsion assembly, paired with a real-fluid pressure assessment of xenon storage across the operating temperature range.

  • SolidWorks
  • NIST fluid data
  • Excel
Read project

At Manastu Space Technologies, I worked on fitting a xenon tank and electric-propulsion components into a compact spacecraft assembly. The task began with the physical layout and mounting structure, then extended to checking whether the tank could hold the required xenon mass across its operating temperature range.

I designed the support structure in SolidWorks and brought the tank, electrical boxes, thruster, and cathode into one assembly. I secured the vertical tank with clamps, placed the electrical boxes alongside it, and mounted the thruster and cathode above it. Working through the complete layout helped me account for the mounting interfaces and how each component's position affected the parts around it.

I produced an assembly drawing with dimensioned orthographic views, an isometric view, and a bill of materials. After the packaging work, I used the specified xenon mass and tank volume to determine the storage density, gathered real-fluid data from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, and plotted pressure against temperature in Excel.

Comparing the highest predicted equilibrium pressure with the tank's stated rating supported the proposed storage conditions on an equilibrium basis. The CAD assembly, drawing, and feasibility report connected the mechanical layout with its operating requirements and strengthened my experience in spacecraft integration.

SimulationSummer 2026

Solenoid Modelling
in ANSYS Maxwell

  • SolidWorks
  • ANSYS Maxwell 3D
  • Magnetostatics

A CAD-to-simulation workflow for a solenoid, building skills relevant to magnetic-circuit analysis for Hall-effect thrusters.

Read project

During my Manastu internship, I modelled a solenoid to learn the ANSYS Maxwell workflow and build skills relevant to Hall-effect thruster magnetic-circuit analysis. I took the model from CAD geometry through simulation setup and magnetic-field visualization.

I created the coil and core in SolidWorks, using a helical path and swept profile for the coil. I kept the bodies separate, left clearance between them, and prepared flat terminal faces before exporting the geometry as a STEP file. In Maxwell, I assigned materials, defined the current terminals, and created the surrounding region for a magnetostatic analysis.

The most useful troubleshooting involved details that were easy to overlook in CAD: body clearance, terminal alignment with the region boundary, and current-path validation. Once the model solved, I used flux-density magnitude and vector plots to examine where the field concentrated and how it was directed.

I documented the setup and post-processing steps in a workflow report for knowledge transfer. The work gave me practical experience with electromagnetic FEA and showed me why a successful solver run is only one step toward quantitative validation, which also needs analytical comparisons and mesh and boundary-sensitivity checks.

University projects

ThermodynamicsWinter 2026

Geothermal Power Plant
& Heat Recovery

Group project

A geothermal generation study for Mongolia's Bayankhongor region, with a heat-pump concept to recover condenser heat for heating.

  • MATLAB
  • Cycle analysis
  • Technical research
Read project

For a group project in MECH 341, we investigated geothermal power generation for Mongolia's Bayankhongor region. We compared a methane-fuelled Rankine cycle with a proposed geothermal plant at Shargaljuut, considering power demand, environmental impact, and the opportunity to reuse waste heat.

My work focused on the environmental comparison and condenser heat recovery. I assessed the CO₂ emissions associated with the methane baseline and compared them with the proposed geothermal system to evaluate the benefit of a lower-carbon generation source.

I also developed a heat-pump concept to raise low-temperature condenser heat to a level suitable for residential or district heating. I considered both the useful heat available and the electricity required by the compressor, since recovering more heat also adds an electrical load to the plant.

This project helped me connect thermodynamic analysis with practical energy decisions. My contribution brought together emissions reduction, waste-heat utilization, and the trade-off between useful heating and the extra electricity needed to provide it.

Design for manufacturingWinter 2026

C-Clamp Design
& Manufacturing

Group project

A manufacturing demonstrator taking a clamp and its mould components from CAD to 3D printing, CNC milling, turning, and assembly.

  • SolidWorks
  • Mastercam
  • CNC machining
  • 3D printing
Read project

In our MECH 360 group project, we designed and manufactured a C-clamp demonstrator and its mould components using 3D printing, CNC milling, and turning. My contribution focused on the milling work: designing the two mould halves and preparing them for CNC manufacture.

I developed the mould geometry in SolidWorks and adapted it to the available foam stock, cutter sizes, and milling capabilities. That meant modifying internal corners, adding fillets for tool access, and checking that the features could be reached with the equipment we had.

I then generated the CNC milling toolpaths in Mastercam. As the geometry changed, I updated both the CAD models and machining strategy so that the mould halves stayed compatible with the rest of the assembly.

The completed mould halves were successfully machined and integrated with the clamp assembly. The project gave me hands-on experience taking a CAD design into a CNC milling process and making design decisions around tooling, machine access, and stock constraints.
